title: Relative abelian-space normalized Poincare data and comparison predicates
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], their represented schemes [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], the represented base $h_S$, natural commutative group structures, identity sections and structural maps [def-sfb-smooth-integral-group-space]. A pointed space over $B$ consists of $p:X\to B$ and $e:B\to X$ with $pe=1_B$. Products, their projections, pairing maps and base changes are the actual sheaf fibre products [def-sfb-space-sheaf-fibre-product]. The represented base is terminal: any two maps $X\to h_S$ are equal. For a morphism $f:X\to B$, let $\operatorname{IsAbelianFamily}(f)$ mean proper, smooth and locally of finite presentation in the chart sense [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], with every geometric fibre represented by an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]; properness includes separatedness, finite type and universal closedness, so local finite presentation here gives finite presentation. For group spaces the scheme fibre inherits its group structure.

Use the canonical small affine etale ringed models and their fixed module equivalences [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model]. A small-model module is a line when its inverse image under that equivalence is locally the structure module, hence on schemes an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Tensor is sheaf tensor and $L^{-1}=\mathcal Hom(L,\mathcal O)$. Use the existing tensor inverse image of modules [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] with its specified composition comparison [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition], its ordinary small-model conjugate [def-sfb-space-derived-tensor-pullback], the fixed unit comparison [def-sfb-space-affine-sections-compositors], and normalized rigidification pullbacks with their specified compositors [def-sfb-rigidified-space-lines]. On a represented scheme, restrict on its identity etale chart by the ordinary Zariski restriction [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]. Define $\operatorname{FibrewiseTrivial}(f,L)$ by requiring on every algebraically closed geometric scheme fibre that this restriction of $L$ be algebraically equivalent to $\mathcal O$ under the existing smooth connected parameter-family equivalence relation [def-sfb-line-algebraic-equivalence].

For pointed $A,D$ over $B$ and $P$ on $A\times_BD$, $\operatorname{Axes}(A,D,P)$ consists of specified trivializations on $e_A\times D$ and $A\times e_D$, with equal induced trivializations on $B$. An isomorphism preserves axes when its two restricted maps commute with those specified trivializations via the canonical tensor compositors. $\operatorname{AxisEquivalent}(A,D,L,M)$ means both modules admit compatible axis trivializations and every pair of such trivializations admits exactly one axis-preserving isomorphism $L\simeq M$. $\operatorname{CanonicalAxisEquivalent}$ additionally requires this assertion after every scheme base change $T\to B$ with $T$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and requires the actual tensor pullback of every normalized isomorphism to preserve the pulled-back axes. This convention includes the tensor and dual-cancellation normalizations. For proper geometrically connected factors it is equivalent to specifying the isomorphism for the canonical axes: units on both factors and their product come from the base.

For $r:\operatorname{Axes}(A,D,P)$, $\operatorname{Represents}(A,D,P,r)$ means that $P$ is a line fibrewise algebraically trivial over $D$, and for every $S$-scheme $T$, map $b:h_T\to B$, fibrewise algebraically trivial line $L$ on $A\times_BT$, and identity rigidification of $L$, there is exactly one map $a:h_T\to D$ over $B$ for which $(1\times a)^*P\simeq L$ preserves the given rigidification. $\operatorname{RigidAutomorphisms}(A)$ means that for every such $T,b$ and every rigidified line, without the algebraic-triviality restriction, an automorphism preserving rigidification is the identity. A dual comparison consists of an isomorphism of the proposed dual spaces over $B$ preserving the identity sections, together with its universal-line isomorphism preserving both axes. $\operatorname{ComparisonCoherence}$ requires a comparison to every other representing datum and uniqueness of that entire comparison, so the identity and composite comparisons agree.

For commutative group spaces $A,D$ over $S$, use their given pointwise laws to define the actual addition maps. A map is a homomorphism when it preserves identity and multiplication on every scheme test. $\operatorname{Biadditive}(A,D,P)$ abbreviates the two canonically axis-preserving identities $(m_A,1)^*P\simeq p_{13}^*P\otimes p_{23}^*P$ on $A\times_SA\times_SD$ and $(1,m_D)^*P\simeq p_{12}^*P\otimes p_{13}^*P$ on $A\times_SD\times_SD$, including their base changes. For any line $L$ on $A$, define the actual module $N_L=m_A^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*L^{-1}\otimes q^*e_A^*L$. $\operatorname{ClassifiesDifference}(L,\phi)$ is its normalized axis-equivalence with $(1\times\phi)^*P$. $\operatorname{DifferenceHomomorphisms}$ requires a unique such $\phi:A\to D$, its homomorphism property, and base-change compatibility of its normalized isomorphism. For $a:A\to B$ and arbitrary abelian dual representing data $(E,Q)$ for $B$, $\operatorname{Dualizes}(a,b)$ is the normalized axis-equivalence $(a\times1)^*Q\simeq(1\times b)^*P$; $\operatorname{DualHomomorphisms}$ requires for every homomorphism $a$ a unique such $b:E\to D$, its homomorphism property and the same compatibility.

Finally $\operatorname{UniversalBaseChange}(A,D,P,r)$ requires for every locally Noetherian scheme $T\to B$ that the actual fibre products $A_T,D_T$ are abelian families, that rigidified line automorphisms on $A_T$ are trivial, and that the actual pullback of $P$ with exactly its pulled-back axes represents the corresponding functor and has unique normalized comparisons with all other representing data. In particular this includes geometric fibres and identity and iterated comparison coherence. These are definitions of data and predicates, not an assertion of existence of a relative dual.
